blocks.text: Ladner Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Fee-simple parcels are the only farm form: Tenure is overwhelmingly freehold; no strata farm complex was confirmed on an official source.

Serviced vs unserviced: under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence and payment of water fees and rentals before lawful use; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. A home or building with indoor plumbing not connected to a community sewer must use an onsite sewage system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, designed/installed/inspected only by an Authorized Person (Professional Engineer or Registered Onsite Wastewater Practitioner), per Fraser Health.
Farm zoning: the A1 Agriculture zone of the Delta Zoning Bylaw (Part 10, Agriculture Zones, as amended by Bylaw 8285, 2023) is the zone intended for farming, breeding pets, kennels and related uses.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Subdivision of farm land (A1, s. 10.10.8): subdivision is not permitted except where it complies with the OCP Bylaw and has been approved under the Agricultural Land Commission Act if applicable; the minimum lot size that may be created by subdivision is 8 ha, with a home site severance exception under ALC policy.
Subdivision servicing: subdivision runs through the City's Approving Officer against the zone minimums and works-and-services conditions, plus ALC approval in the ALR.

Farm classification is earned by income, not by zoning: A parcel can be A1-zoned, Agriculture (A)-designated and in the ALR and still lose farm class if the operation (or its lease) cannot meet BC Assessment's size-scaled gross income thresholds — sellers who document the farm income history, leases, water licences and ALC approvals in place hold the items a farm buyer's lender and lawyer ask for first.

The farm home plate is the hidden cap: Beyond the 500 m² house limit, Delta's A1 zone caps the whole farm home plate at 3,600 m² (5,000 m² with an additional farm house on it) — the plate, not the lot, is what a large-house-plus-yard plan actually runs into.

Migrant worker housing has a two-size test most buyers miss: The employing farm must be at least 8 ha AND the lot at least 4 ha, with ALR status, farm classification and written ALC approval all in place — and new buildings must be manufactured homes on a temporary foundation or footings.

faq.a: Non-domestic groundwater use (including irrigation) requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act, with fees and rentals, before lawful use. The parcel's ditch/drainage irrigation arrangements with the City: unconfirmed — get them from the City, not from a listing.

faq.q: Is Ladner farmland the same market as East Delta?
faq.a: On this page, yes in practice: the live ladner-farms feed carried both Ladner Rural and East Delta sub-area listings, and both sit under the same rules — Delta's Official Community Plan Agriculture (A) designation and A1 zoning where the zone applies.

faq.q: Can a Ladner-area farm have a second dwelling?
faq.a: Yes, within limits: Delta's A1 zone permits one accessory farm dwelling unit per lot — 90 m² or less on lots of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger lots — on the same farm home plate as the farm house; more than one needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and an additional farm house needs an agrologist's necessity report plus written ALC approval.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a Delta farm parcel?
faq.a: Only within tight limits: in the A1 zone a new lot created by subdivision needs a minimum of 8 ha, Official Community Plan compliance and Agricultural Land Commission Act approval where applicable, with a home site severance exception under ALC policy.
